comparisons.peer_summary: Putative class action complaints asserting securities violations were consolidated as IN RE CITIGROUP SECURITIES LITIGATION; the court granted the motion to dismiss without prejudice in March 2023, and plaintiffs subsequently moved for leave to file a second amended complaint in May 2023.
comparisons.comparison: Both Goldman Sachs and Citigroup faced securities class actions where the courts granted motions to dismiss, but the procedural outcomes differed significantly. Goldman Sachs had its second amended complaints dismissed 'with prejudice' in March 2024, though plaintiffs appealed to the Second Circuit. In contrast, Citigroup had its initial complaints dismissed 'without prejudice' in March 2023, allowing plaintiffs to move for leave to file a second amended complaint in May 2023. Both entities were sued for alleged violations of Sections 10(b) and 20(a) of the Exchange Act in the Southern District of New York.

sentences.text: In May 2023, the plaintiffs in the class actions filed second amended complaints, and on March 28, 2024, the court granted the defendants' motion to dismiss the second amended complaints with prejudice.
The complaints generally assert violations of Sections 10(b), 20A and 20(a) of the Exchange Act and seek unspecified damages.
On March 24, 2023, the court granted defendants' motion to dismiss without prejudice.

On May 24, 2023, plaintiffs moved for leave to file a second amended complaint against Citigroup and certain of Citigroup's current or former officers for alleged violations of Sections 10(b) and 20(a) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 based on alleged misstatements concerning risk management and internal controls.
